purpose: A factual record of whether each B1 target's terms could be acquired by an automated request, and on what evidence. It records observations, never conclusions: no entry here grants permission to fetch, to retain, or to use anything, and no entry here is a legal review.

outcomeVocabulary.AUTO_FETCH_REFUSED: The source's own published terms carry an explicit prohibition on automated access, or robots.txt Disallows the path. Requires a verbatim quotation.
outcomeVocabulary.AUTO_FETCH_DEFERRED_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE: The policy could not be read at all -- robots.txt absent, non-2xx, or the host refused the request. Unknown, NOT prohibited.
outcomeVocabulary.AUTO_FETCH_PERMITTED_BY_BASIS: Reachable only with an explicit recorded authorization that resolves to a real basis record carrying the ACQUISITION capability. No entry currently holds it.
outcomeVocabulary.AUTO_FETCH_POLICY_UNVERIFIED: A prohibition has been asserted but the primary source was never opened. Records an unverified claim as unverified. Constrains nothing.

invariants: A robots.txt 'Allow' is ONE POSITIVE SIGNAL and can never by itself produce AUTO_FETCH_PERMITTED_BY_BASIS. Both hosts below allow, and both are still REFUSED, because the terms are the stronger instrument and they say otherwise.
A robots.txt 403 is POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and can never produce AUTO_FETCH_REFUSED. A host that will not show you its policy has not stated one.

An outcome of AUTO_FETCH_REFUSED requires a verbatim quotation with its section heading. A paraphrase, a summary, or another agent's characterisation is not sufficient and must be recorded as AUTO_FETCH_POLICY_UNVERIFIED instead.

evidenceMethods.ROBOTS_PARSER_PROBE: urllib.robotparser against the live host. Records status, byte length and the can_fetch verdict for the target path.
evidenceMethods.WEB_FETCH_MARKDOWN_EXTRACTION: The page was fetched, converted to markdown, and the clause extracted by a model. This yields TEXT, not bytes: no sha256 is recorded and none may be inferred. Weaker than a byte-exact capture and deliberately labelled so.
evidenceMethods.COMMITTED_REPOSITORY_DOCUMENT: A document already committed in this repository.

observations.reason: www.technogym.com returns HTTP 403 to programmatic requests, robots.txt included, so its automated-access policy cannot be read. Unknown, not prohibited -- and not a reason to substitute a User-Agent or retry.
observations.termsDocumentUrlNote: Not discoverable: the host refuses programmatic requests.

evidence.result: SEARCH_INDEX_SNIPPET only -- technogym.com returned HTTP 403 on every direct attempt (product page, category page, a regional variant, robots.txt, a support-download endpoint)

observations.reason: The published Terms of Use prohibit unauthorised automated access. Note the word 'unauthorised': this is a prohibition on UNAUTHORISED automation, so an authorization is contemplated by the document itself and would change this outcome. None is held today.
observations.termsDocumentUrlNote: A second document exists at https://www.lifefitness.com/en-us/legal/terms-conditions. Which one governs is a legal question B1 does not answer.
observations.documentBytesNote: Operator decision 2026-09-10: option C -- observe and record, retain no bytes. The copying clause below is why the choice mattered.

evidence.result: HTTP 200, 1045 bytes, can_fetch('SPTR-terms-capture')=True, can_fetch('*')=True -- a positive signal that does NOT grant permission

pendingAuthorizations.observation: Salesforce Experience Cloud portal. Root returns an empty client-rendered shell; /s/ returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized. The operator has requested official access.
pendingAuthorizations.note: A REQUEST is not a grant. This entry exists so the request is not forgotten, and it must never be read as an authorization. If access is granted, the portal's own terms -- not the public www terms quoted above -- become the governing document for what that account may do, and a basis record would be written then, not now.
